Used in Arabia before Islam: ʿAbla, the beloved addressed in ʿAntara's Muʿallaqa, 6th century. Written عبلة. (Muʿallaqa of ʿAntara)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Amina bint Wahb of Quraysh, mother of Muhammad, d. c. 577, 6th century. Written آمنة. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Arwa bint ʿAbd al-Muttalib of Quraysh, 6th century. Written أروى. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol. 8)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Asmaʾ, the departing beloved in the first line of al-Harith ibn Hilliza's Muʿallaqa, 6th century. Written أسماء. (Muʿallaqa of al-Harith ibn Hilliza)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Atika bint ʿAbd al-Muttalib of Quraysh, 6th century. Written عاتكة. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)

Used in Arabia before Islam: Fakhita bint Abi Talib (Umm Hani) of Quraysh, born before 610, 6th–7th century. Written فاختة. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol. 8)

Used in Arabia before Islam: Fatima, the beloved addressed in Imruʾ al-Qays's Muʿallaqa; also Fatima bint Asad of Quraysh, b. c. 555, 6th century. Written فاطمة. (Muʿallaqa of Imruʾ al-Qays meaning: Lane)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Hafsa bint ʿUmar of Quraysh, b. c. 605, 7th century. Written حفصة. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol. 8)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Hala bint Khuwaylid of Quraysh, sister of Khadija, 6th century. Written هالة. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol. 8; meaning: Lane)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Halima of Banu Saʿd ibn Bakr, Muhammad's foster-mother, 6th century. Written حليمة. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya (fosterage among Banu Saʿd); meaning: Lane)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Hamna bint Jahsh of Asad ibn Khuzayma, born before 610, 6th–7th century. Written حمنة. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol. 8)

Used in Arabia before Islam: Hind, mother of the Lakhmid king ʿAmr ibn Hind (r. 554–569), named in ʿAmr ibn Kulthum's Muʿallaqa, 6th century. Written هند. (Muʿallaqa of ʿAmr ibn Kulthum meaning: Lane, Arabic-English Lexicon)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Kabsha, daughter of ʿUrwa al-Rahhal of Kilab, mother of the chief ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl, 6th century. Written كبشة. (Lyall, The Mufaddaliyat vol. II (1918))

Used in Arabia before Islam: Layla bint al-Muhalhil of Taghlib, mother of the poet ʿAmr ibn Kulthum (not in the Muʿallaqat), 6th century. Written ليلى. (Lyall, The Mufaddaliyat vol. II (1918), notes citing Kitab al-Aghani)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Lubaba bint al-Harith (Umm al-Fadl) of Hilal, b. c. 593, 6th century. Written لبابة. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Nawar, the beloved in Labid's Muʿallaqa, 6th century. Written نوار. (Muʿallaqa of Labid)

Used in Arabia before Islam: al-Rabab, known in Imruʾ al-Qays's Muʿallaqa only through the by-name Umm al-Rabab; a nasib name in the Mufaddaliyyat, 6th century. Written رباب. (Muʿallaqa of Imruʾ al-Qays Lyall, The Mufaddaliyat vol. II (1918))
Used in Arabia before Islam: Ramla bint Abi Sufyan (Umm Habiba) of Quraysh, b. c. 594, 6th century. Written رملة. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol. 8; meaning: Lane)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Rayhana bint Zayd of the Banu Nadir, born before 610, 6th–7th century. Written ريحانة. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra)

Used in Arabia before Islam: Salma bint ʿAmr of Banu al-Najjar, mother of ʿAbd al-Muttalib; also the beloved in al-Musayyab ibn ʿAlas's ode, 5th–6th century. Written سلمى. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya; Lyall, The Mufaddaliyat vol. II (1918))
Used in Arabia before Islam: Sawda bint Zamʿa of Quraysh, born before 610, 6th century. Written سودة. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol. 8)
Used in Arabia before Islam: al-Shifaʾ bint ʿAbd Allah of ʿAdi, Quraysh, born before 610, 6th–7th century. Written الشفاء. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol. 8)
Used in Arabia before Islam: al-ʿAbbas ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib of Quraysh, b. c. 568, 6th century. Written عباس. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, father of Muhammad, c. 545–570, 6th century. Written عبد الله. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: ʿAbid ibn al-Abras of Asad, poet whose ode is counted among the ten Muʿallaqat, 6th century. Written عبيد. (the Muʿallaqat)
Used in Arabia before Islam: ʿAdi ibn Zayd, Christian poet of al-Hira, d. c. 600 (not in the Muʿallaqat), 6th century. Written عدي. (Kitab al-Aghani; Lyall, The Mufaddaliyat vol. II (1918))
Used in Arabia before Islam: ʿAdnan, ancestor of the northern Arabs in the genealogies, traditional genealogy. Written عدنان. (Ibn Hazm, Jamharat Ansab al-ʿArab; Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: ʿAli ibn Abi Talib of Quraysh, b. c. 600, 7th century. Written علي. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl, chief and poet of ʿAmir ibn Saʿsaʿa, 6th–7th century. Written عامر. (Kitab al-Aghani; Lyall, The Mufaddaliyat vol. II (1918))
Used in Arabia before Islam: ʿAmmar ibn Yasir of Mecca, b. c. 567, 6th century. Written عمار. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Asad ibn Hashim of Quraysh, 6th century. Written أسد. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya; meaning: Lane)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Bilal ibn Rabah of Mecca, b. c. 580, 6th century. Written بلال. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Hakim ibn Hizam of Quraysh, Khadija's nephew, b. c. 570s, 6th century. Written حكيم. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Hamza ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib of Quraysh, b. c. 568, 6th century. Written حمزة. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Hani ibn Masʿud of Shayban, a chief at the Battle of Dhu Qar, c. 609, 7th century. Written هانئ. (al-Tabari, Tarikh al-Rusul wa-l-Muluk)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Harb ibn Umayya, chief of Quraysh, 6th century. Written حرب. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: al-Harith ibn Hilliza of Yashkur, poet of a Muʿallaqa, 6th century. Written حارث. (the Muʿallaqat meaning: Lane)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Hashim ibn ʿAbd Manaf, chief of Quraysh, 5th century. Written هاشم. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Hassan ibn Thabit of Yathrib, poet before Islam, b. c. 563, 6th century. Written حسان. (Kitab al-Aghani)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Hatim al-Taʾi, chief and poet of Tayyiʾ, 6th century. Written حاتم. (Kitab al-Aghani)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Hilal ibn ʿAmir, eponym of the Banu Hilal, traditional genealogy. Written هلال. (Ibn Hazm, Jamharat Ansab al-ʿArab)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Hisham ibn al-Mughira, chief of Makhzum, 6th century. Written هشام. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Ilyas ibn Mudar, ancestor in the genealogies, traditional genealogy. Written إلياس. (Ibn Hazm, Jamharat Ansab al-ʿArab)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Kinana ibn Khuzayma, ancestor of Quraysh in the genealogies, traditional genealogy. Written كنانة. (Ibn Hazm, Jamharat Ansab al-ʿArab; Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Labid ibn Rabiʿa of ʿAmir, poet of a Muʿallaqa, b. c. 560, 6th century. Written لبيد. (the Muʿallaqat)

Used in Arabia before Islam: the Nabataean kings Malichus I and II (Nabataean mlkw, Maliku); also Tarafa's cousin Malik in his Muʿallaqa, 1st century BCE–1st century CE. Written مالك. (Nabataean coins and inscriptions Muʿallaqa of Tarafa)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Mudar ibn Nizar, ancestor in the genealogies, traditional genealogy. Written مضر. (Ibn Hazm, Jamharat Ansab al-ʿArab)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Nawfal ibn ʿAbd Manaf of Quraysh, 6th century. Written نوفل. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Nizar ibn Maʿadd, ancestor in the genealogies, traditional genealogy. Written نزار. (Ibn Hazm, Jamharat Ansab al-ʿArab)
Used in Arabia before Islam: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab of Quraysh, b. c. 584, 6th century. Written عمر. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Talib ibn Abi Talib of Quraysh, 6th century. Written طالب. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)

Used in Arabia before Islam: Yasir ibn ʿAmir of Madhhij, settled at Mecca, 6th century. Written ياسر. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Yazid of Banu Shayban, addressed in al-Aʿsha's Muʿallaqa, 6th–7th century. Written يزيد. (Muʿallaqa of al-Aʿsha)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Queen Huldu, wife of the Nabataean king Aretas IV, on coins and inscriptions, 1st century BCE–1st century CE. Written خلدو. (Nabataean coins and inscriptions)

Used in Arabia before Islam: Hurayra, a singing-girl celebrated in the first line of al-Aʿsha's Muʿallaqa, 6th–7th century. Written هريرة. (Muʿallaqa of al-Aʿsha Lyall, The Mufaddaliyat vol. II (1918))
Used in Arabia before Islam: Khadija bint Khuwaylid of Quraysh, c. 555–619, 6th century. Written خديجة. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol. 8; Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: al-Khansaʾ (Tumadir bint ʿAmr) of Sulaym, poet, b. c. 575; a by-name, 6th century. Written الخنساء. (Ibn Sallam, Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shuʿaraʾ; Kitab al-Aghani)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Khawla, the beloved in the first line of Tarafa's Muʿallaqa; also a nasib name in the Mufaddaliyyat, 6th century. Written خولة. (Muʿallaqa of Tarafa)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Maymuna bint al-Harith of Hilal, b. c. 594, 6th century. Written ميمونة. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol. 8)

Used in Arabia before Islam: Mawiyya (Mavia), queen of the Tanukh, 4th c.; also Mawiyya, wife of Hatim al-Taʾi, 4th century. Written ماوية. (Sozomen and Socrates Scholasticus, Ecclesiastical History; Kitab al-Aghani)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Mayya, the beloved in the first line of al-Nabigha's Muʿallaqa, 6th century. Written مية. (Muʿallaqa of al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Naʾila of Jurhum, of the legend of Isaf and Naʾila at Mecca, pre-Islamic legend. Written نائلة. (Ibn al-Kalbi, Kitab al-Asnam)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Ruqayya, daughter of Muhammad and Khadija, b. c. 601, 7th century. Written رقية. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol. 8)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Safiyya bint ʿAbd al-Muttalib of Quraysh, b. c. 569, 6th century. Written صفية. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol. 8)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Sumayya bint Khayyat of Mecca, d. c. 615, 6th century. Written سمية. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol. 8)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Umayma bint ʿAbd al-Muttalib of Quraysh, 6th century. Written أميمة. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol. 8)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Umama, wife of the poet al-Jumayh of Asad, addressed in his ode of c. 570, 6th century. Written أمامة. (Mufaddaliyyat; Lyall, The Mufaddaliyat vol. II (1918))

Used in Arabia before Islam: Zaynab bint Jahsh, b. c. 590; also a nasib name in a pre-Islamic ode of the Mufaddaliyyat, 6th century. Written زينب. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol. 8; Lyall, The Mufaddaliyat vol. II (1918))
Used in Arabia before Islam: Zarqaʾ al-Yamama of Jadis, the far-sighted woman of legend; a by-name, pre-Islamic legend. Written زرقاء. (later medieval akhbar on the Jahiliyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: ʿAntara ibn Shaddad of ʿAbs, poet of a Muʿallaqa, 6th century. Written عنترة. (the Muʿallaqat)
Used in Arabia before Islam: ʿAqil ibn Abi Talib of Quraysh, 6th century. Written عقيل. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Durayd ibn al-Simma of Jusham, poet and war-leader, 6th century. Written دريد. (Kitab al-Aghani)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Fihr ibn Malik, ancestor of Quraysh in the genealogies, traditional genealogy. Written فهر. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Ghalib ibn Fihr, ancestor of Quraysh in the genealogies, traditional genealogy. Written غالب. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Jaʿfar ibn Abi Talib of Quraysh, b. c. 590, 6th century. Written جعفر. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya; meaning: Lane)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Jubayr ibn Mutʿim of Nawfal, Quraysh, born before 610, 6th century. Written جبير. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Qays ibn Khalid of Shayban, named in Tarafa's Muʿallaqa; a chief Qays is also named in al-Harith ibn Hilliza's, 6th century. Written قيس. (Muʿallaqa of Tarafa)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Khalid of Shayban, father of Qays ibn Khalid, named in Tarafa's Muʿallaqa, 6th century. Written خالد. (Muʿallaqa of Tarafa meaning: Lane)
Used in Arabia before Islam: al-Khattab ibn Nufayl of ʿAdi, Quraysh, father of ʿUmar, 6th century. Written الخطاب. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Kilab ibn Murra of Quraysh, father of Qusayy, 5th century. Written كلاب. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Kulayb ibn Rabiʿa of Taghlib, whose killing began the War of al-Basus, 5th–6th century. Written كليب. (Kitab al-Aghani)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Maymun ibn Qays, the poet al-Aʿsha, d. c. 625, 6th century. Written ميمون. (Kitab al-Aghani)
Used in Arabia before Islam: al-Mundhir III ibn Maʾ al-Samaʾ, Lakhmid king, named in al-Harith ibn Hilliza's Muʿallaqa, 6th century. Written المنذر. (Muʿallaqa of al-Harith ibn Hilliza)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Musʿab ibn ʿUmayr of Quraysh, b. c. 585, 6th century. Written مصعب. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra)
Used in Arabia before Islam: al-Nuʿman III, Lakhmid king of al-Hira, named in al-Nabigha's Muʿallaqa, 6th century. Written النعمان. (Muʿallaqa of al-Nabigha)
Used in Arabia before Islam: ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan of Quraysh, b. c. 576, 6th century. Written عثمان. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Qahtan, ancestor of the southern Arabs in the genealogies, traditional genealogy. Written قحطان. (Ibn Hazm, Jamharat Ansab al-ʿArab)
Used in Arabia before Islam: al-Qasim, son of Muhammad and Khadija, b. c. 598, 6th century. Written القاسم. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Qusayy ibn Kilab, chief of Quraysh at Mecca, 5th century. Written قصي. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: the Nabataean kings Rabbel I and Rabbel II (r. 70–106), on coins and inscriptions, 1st century BCE–2nd century CE. Written رب إيل. (Nabataean coins and inscriptions)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas of Quraysh, b. c. 595, 6th century. Written سعد. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Saʿid ibn Zayd of Quraysh, b. c. 593, 6th century. Written سعيد. (Ibn Saʿd, al-Tabaqat al-Kubra)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Sakhr ibn ʿAmr of Sulaym, brother of al-Khansaʾ, 6th century. Written صخر. (Kitab al-Aghani)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Shaddad of ʿAbs, father of the poet ʿAntara, 6th century. Written شداد. (Kitab al-Aghani)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Shayba ibn Rabiʿa of ʿAbd Shams; also the birth name of ʿAbd al-Muttalib, 6th century. Written شيبة. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Suhayl ibn ʿAmr of Quraysh, born before 610, 6th century. Written سهيل. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya; meaning: Lane)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Tarafa ibn al-ʿAbd of Bakr, poet of a Muʿallaqa, 6th century. Written طرفة. (the Muʿallaqat)

Used in Arabia before Islam: al-Tufayl ibn Malik of ʿAmir, father of the chief ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl, 6th century. Written الطفيل. (Lyall, The Mufaddaliyat vol. II (1918); Kitab al-Aghani)
Used in Arabia before Islam: ʿUtba ibn Rabiʿa, chief of ʿAbd Shams, 6th century. Written عتبة. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Wahb ibn ʿAbd Manaf of Zuhra, father of Amina, 6th century. Written وهب. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl of Quraysh, a hanif, d. c. 605, 6th century. Written زيد. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Ziyad ibn Muʿawiya, the poet al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani, 6th century. Written زياد. (Ibn Sallam, Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shuʿaraʾ; Kitab al-Aghani)
Used in Arabia before Islam: al-Zubayr ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib of Quraysh, poet, 6th century. Written الزبير. (Ibn Hisham, al-Sira al-Nabawiyya)
Used in Arabia before Islam: Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma of Muzayna, poet of a Muʿallaqa, 6th century. Written زهير. (the Muʿallaqat)
